bear.text: EBITDA margin contracted by 170 basis points to 11.2% in Q1 FY27, driven by a sharp rise in copper prices.
Receivable days increased from 78 to 96 over the last year, primarily due to slower payments from two large state utility customers.
The company received a GST demand order for ₹46.3 crore relating to input tax credits claimed for FY2020-21 and FY2021-22.

bull.text: Revenue from operations grew 18.0% year-over-year to ₹1,248 crore in Q1 FY27.
The order book stood at ₹3,900 crore as of 30 June 2026, up from ₹3,150 crore a year ago.
Management states the new Bharuch plant is on track to begin commercial production in Q3 FY27, adding about 30% to cable capacity.
Exports contributed 21% of revenue in Q1 FY27, up from 16% in the same period last year.

open_questions.text: The company's press release reports Q1 FY27 revenue of ₹1,248 crore, while a news article reports ₹1,428 crore. Which figure is accurate?
Management intends to appeal the GST demand and expects no material impact, but what is the likelihood of a successful appeal?
Management expects to pass on higher copper costs over the next two quarters, but how effective will this be given the lag in price-variation clauses?

snapshot.text: Sarvottam Cables Ltd is a manufacturer of power cables, wires and conductors.
In Q1 FY27, the company reported revenue of ₹1,248 crore and profit after tax of ₹82 crore.
As of June 2026, promoters held 58.2% of the company, with 4.1% of that holding pledged.
